routes.label: California, US
routes.pathway: Conventional US MD → family medicine residency
routes.reason: Public board rules explicitly separate initial unrestricted licensure from residency completion and continuing renewal requirements.
routes.notes: Four-year college and four-year MD are conventional route assumptions, not a California statutory minimum. US and Canadian graduates need 12 months of approved postgraduate training; international graduates have a different rule. The family medicine residency totals three years including its first year. Initial licence renewal requires 36 months or continued enrolment, followed by later verification. Board certification is a specialty credential, not a universal legal condition for a general medical licence.
routes.evidence_status: Core licence and residency requirements read; conventional degree duration from indexed AAMC guidance

stages.label: USMLE Steps 1 and 2CK

routes.label: England
routes.pathway: Standard undergraduate medicine → Foundation → GP training
routes.reason: Standard five-year route with an explicit distinction between provisional registration, full registration and GP qualification.
routes.notes: Five-year degree is the selected standard route; four-year graduate-entry courses need prior education. Full registration after Foundation year 1 does not qualify a doctor for independent NHS general practice. The three-year GP programme is a later specialty route. CCT, GP Register and applicable NHS performers-list requirements remain conditions, rather than zero-time guarantees.
routes.evidence_status: GMC route, curriculum and NHS programme guidance read

stages.label: Medical degree
stages.note: Standard five-year undergraduate route.

stages.label: Medical Licensing Assessment

stages.label: Provisional registration
stages.note: Registration with licence for Foundation year 1.

stages.label: Foundation year 1
stages.note: Supervised first foundation year.

stages.label: Full registration

stages.label: Foundation year 2

routes.label: Bavaria, Germany
routes.reason: Federal law specifies a standard course including examination time, and Bavaria provides binding regional GP specialty rules. School baseline uses Bavaria's nine-year Gymnasium.
routes.notes: Six years three months is the statutory standard course including the final examination period, not an observed average or an invariant earliest possible completion. The 48-week practical year is embedded and must not be added again. Approbation is the first general medical licence. The GP specialist qualification requires five more years and examination; statutory-insurance participation and setting up a practice have further conditions.

stages.label: Medical course and state examinations

stages.label: Embedded practical year (48 weeks)

stages.label: Medical state examinations passed

stages.label: Approbation

stages.label: GP specialist training complete

routes.label: Japan
routes.pathway: Medicine → initial clinical training → general practice specialty
routes.reason: Ministry diagrams distinguish the medical licence from completion of mandatory initial clinical training; current facility-management rules add a separate role requirement.
routes.notes: The licence follows six-year medical education and the national examination. Clinical practice then requires at least two years of initial clinical training. Completion is not itself the opening of an insured clinic. For people who had not completed initial training by 1 April 2026, the standard facility-manager route adds three years of insured hospital practice; alternative and transitional rules exist. The main later-training route is the Japanese Medical Specialty Board general practice (総合診療) specialty, requiring at least three years. Board examination and certification remain additional conditions.
routes.evidence_status: Current Japanese Act licensing clauses, ministry route diagram and relevant JMSB general-practice standards read

stages.label: Medical degree
stages.note: Six-year undergraduate medical programme.

stages.label: National medical examination
stages.note: Required for licence; examination and registration wait not separately estimated. Domestic graduates also need the pre-clerkship common examination under Article 11; it is embedded in medical education.

stages.label: Medical licence and registration
stages.note: First medical licence; mandatory clinical training remains ahead.

stages.label: Medical licence
stages.note: Same licence event; a UK-style full/provisional distinction is not imposed on Japan.

stages.label: Mandatory initial clinical training
stages.note: At least two years; clinically supervised training follows the medical licence.

stages.label: Initial clinical training complete
stages.note: Clinical-training endpoint after eight post-school years; not equivalent to a GP specialist certificate or insured-facility manager eligibility.

stages.label: General practice specialty training (総合診療)
stages.note: At least three years after initial clinical training; required rotations, competence and completion review apply. The general practice specialty is distinct from internal medicine.

stages.label: General practice specialty assessment
stages.note: Completed training and the Board certification examination are distinct requirements; examination or registration waits are not estimated.

stages.label: General practice specialty training complete
stages.note: Family/general-practice training endpoint at eleven post-school years on this selected minimum route; specialist certification also requires the Board examination.

stages.label: Insured facility manager — standard experience route
stages.note: Three years of insured hospital practice after initial training for the specified new cohort. Alternative eligibility and transition rules apply. Can overlap specialty experience; never add both bars.

routes.label: India
routes.pathway: MBBS → internship → optional MD Family Medicine
routes.reason: National regulations distinguish academic MBBS study, internship and the permanent registration that permits independent general medical practice.
routes.notes: The academic phase is 54 months and the internship twelve months. Passing final academic examinations permits provisional internship registration, not independent practice. Permanent registration follows internship and other eligibility conditions. The optional MD Family Medicine route is three years after MBBS/internship for a candidate without an existing relevant postgraduate diploma. An NMC permission letter for CMC Vellore confirms that the regulator authorises this qualification; access to a place is not assumed universal. NExT was notified and deferred; it is not modelled as an operating extra examination year. The original NMC curriculum, internship regulation and deferral notice were retrieved. No later NExT commencement notice was found in the current rules index and bounded news search on 22 November 2026; rules applying to a future cohort can change.
routes.evidence_status: Original NMC curriculum, internship and postgraduate regulations and deferral notice read in relevant sections; legacy provisional-registration provision corroborated by government hospital practice

stages.label: MBBS academic phase
stages.note: Four and a half years; the full route includes the following internship. Do not label this alone the completed qualification.

stages.label: Final MBBS academic examinations
stages.note: Examinations are within the academic phase. NExT deferral is not treated as proof of a new operational examination route.

stages.label: Provisional internship registration
stages.note: Provisional internship registration follows the final MBBS pass certificate. The national procedural provision is corroborated by official hospital implementation; state administration and processing vary.

stages.label: Compulsory rotating internship
stages.note: At least twelve months before permanent registration.

stages.label: Permanent registration
stages.note: Enables independent general medical practice subject to the registration conditions; no residency assumed necessary for this general licence.

stages.label: Independent general medical practice eligibility
stages.note: Same point as permanent registration; not a specialist qualification or a guarantee that all state/institutional service obligations are fulfilled.

stages.label: Optional MD Family Medicine
stages.note: NMC authorised MD Family Medicine at the selected institution. Three-year postgraduate broad-specialty route for a candidate without a relevant prior diploma; not required for a general medical licence.

stages.label: MD Family Medicine final assessment
stages.note: Assessment is included in the three-year degree period; successful completion is required for the qualification.

stages.label: MD Family Medicine training complete
stages.note: Selected family-medicine qualification endpoint after eight and a half post-school years. Current admission availability, service obligations and award administration are not modelled.

routes.label: Singapore
routes.pathway: NTU MBBS → PGY1 → family medicine residency
routes.reason: Selected local undergraduate route, whose full-registration rules differ from those for overseas graduates.
routes.notes: The five-year NTU degree is an explicitly selected local route; Duke-NUS graduate-entry medicine has prior-degree requirements. Provisional registration covers twelve months of PGY1. Eligible local graduates may apply for full registration after satisfactory PGY1; a practising certificate is also needed. Full registration permits independent practice; family-physician accreditation is a separate credential. The main later-training bar is the three-year family-medicine residency. Completion is distinct from Family Physician accreditation, which also requires a relevant qualification, recognised FM practice experience and currency of practice; relevant residency postings may count. A new family-medicine specialist route is planned for 2028 and is not applied retrospectively. National Service and admission gaps are not included in the academic clock.
routes.evidence_status: Programme, registration and specialist-accreditation guidance read

stages.label: NTU MBBS
stages.note: Five-year local undergraduate medical programme.

stages.label: Medical degree assessments passed
stages.note: Local qualification prerequisite; no separate extra licensing-examination period added to the selected route.

stages.label: Provisional registration
stages.note: Local graduate registration for PGY1 in approved hospitals.

stages.label: PGY1 housemanship
stages.note: Twelve months, with satisfactory completion documented by certificate of experience.

stages.label: Full registration
stages.note: Eligibility to apply after PGY1 for the selected local route; issue and practising-certificate processing not estimated.

stages.label: Independent general medical practice eligibility
stages.note: Full registration permits independent practice; this is not specialist or family-physician accreditation.

stages.label: Family medicine residency
stages.note: Three years after PGY1 on the selected current entry route. Does not add another three years of experience automatically; relevant residency postings may count toward accreditation.

stages.label: Family medicine training assessments
stages.note: Training includes assessments. The postgraduate qualification and FPAB experience/currency conditions must be met for Family Physician registration; completion alone does not guarantee accreditation.

stages.label: Family medicine residency complete
stages.note: Family-medicine training endpoint at nine post-school years. A relevant qualification, recognised FM experience and currency of practice are separate accreditation conditions.
